findings.where: 'Good for' section: the 13 chips (First-time surfers … Sunsets), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The chips are filled pills with outlines, the shape and edge of filter chips. They are static (parts p6-p17), so tapping 'Budget' or 'Solo travellers' does nothing. On a 'Best Hostels' page with no listings, they look like the way to narrow down hostels.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on their phone who taps 'Budget' expecting cheaper hostels, gets nothing, and decides the page is broken

findings.fault: The chips are a rainbow of off-palette colours: hot pink, purple, crimson-coral, yellow, green and teal. Each fill has a clashing border (yellow with pink, pink with blue, purple with dark violet). The colours carry no meaning, and some are coral-like fills used as decoration. This loud patch sits mid-page in a reading section and outshouts the h1.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the brand gives every colour one job, keeps coral for CTAs only and has no pink or purple. A visitor who looks for a meaning in the colours finds none.

findings.fault: 'Vibe' is set in italic turquoise with an underline, so it looks like a link, but it is static (p5). It is also treated differently from its sibling heading 'Surf', which is plain ink, and it sets type in a fill colour.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who taps 'Vibe' expecting more about the scene and nothing happens; the founder, because the underline and link colour are reserved for links

findings.where: 'Coming soon' announcement block above the footer, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The notice sits on a saturated crimson ground that reads as an error or warning alert. The brand names the ink night ground for the interior announcement. On desktop the text fills only the left half of a full-width red slab, which leaves a large empty red area.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who sees a red box and thinks something failed or the destination is unavailable; the founder, whose rules put this block on ink and keep red for errors and sold-out states

findings.where: h1 'Best Hostels in Canggu' against the page content
findings.fault: The heading promises a list of the best hostels. The page names no hostel and gives no ranking; it is a short area overview. The h1 is also in title case, not sentence case.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who arrives from a search for 'best hostels Canggu' and finds no hostels feels misled and leaves; the founder's honesty principle and the sentence-case rule

findings.where: Nav 'Destinations' and 'How we rank'; footer Privacy, Terms, How we rank, Report content
findings.fault: Every page link goes nowhere. 'How we rank', Privacy, Terms and Report content all link back to this same page (p4, p21-p24). 'Destinations' jumps to #destinations, but the render shows no destinations section. Only the email works.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who checks 'How we rank' to see whether the ranking can be trusted, or wants the privacy terms, and lands back at the top of the same page; this hurts trust on a brand whose product is trust

findings.fault: The page has no next step. The announcement says listings are coming but offers nothing to do: no link to a live destination, no way to be told when listings arrive, no way back to the guide index. The page dead-ends.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has decided Canggu suits them and wants to act next, and the founder, who loses the visitor at that moment

findings.where: Body text throughout: the intro, Surf, Vibe, What to look for and the announcement, worst on phone
findings.fault: Body copy is fully justified. At the narrow column this opens wide gaps between words ('MantaHostels   is   launching   across', 'workers   and   long-stay') and makes the text uneven to read.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader scanning mid-transit, whose eye stumbles on the gaps; it also looks unpolished next to the brand's 'effortless' first feeling

findings.where: Section headings: 'Surf', 'Vibe', 'Good for', 'What to look for'
findings.fault: Four sibling sections use three heading treatments: plain Quicksand for Surf and Good for, italic underlined turquoise for Vibe, and small letter-spaced uppercase for What to look for. 'What to look for', the section that delivers the page's stated purpose, gets the weakest heading. The house reserves uppercase for badges and filter labels.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the page, who reads the treatments as different levels and finds the section they came for underplayed

findings.where: Top of the page (first screen), desktop and phone
findings.fault: The destination page has no hero banner: no turquoise ground, no illustration and no loud moment, only a sand page with a small h1. The only loud object is the rainbow chip block halfway down, so the energy sits in the wrong place.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the brand names destination-page top banners as the loud marketing zone and calls sterile the enemy; a first-time visitor gets little feeling for Canggu

findings.where: Desktop layout: the content column against the chip row and announcement
findings.fault: The text sits in a narrow left column with more than half the 1440 px screen empty sand to its right. The chip rows and the announcement run the full container width, so the page has no consistent right edge and looks unfinished.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor planning a trip, who sees a lopsided page that looks half-built

findings.fault: The section that serves the page's stated job (what to look for in a Canggu hostel) is one sentence, the thinnest on the page. It gives nothing on which area suits whom (Berawa, Batu Bolong, Echo Beach), getting around, or what dorms cost.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker trying to judge which part of Canggu and which kind of hostel suits them, who still can't decide after reading

findings.fault: When the links wrap on phone, a stray '·' separator hangs at the end of the first line after 'How we rank'.
findings.who_objects: Few would notice; it reads as a careless line break
